html:
The Cariban languages are a family of about three dozen languages of northern South America, from the mouth of the Amazon to the Colombian Andes. Most have only a few hundred speakers; Macushi, with about 30,000, is the largest.

The family is named after the Carib-speaking Kalina of the Guiana coast. The island Kalinago took the Carib name, though their everyday language was Arawakan.

Cariban peoples on the chart include the Pemón of Venezuela, the Patamona of Guyana, the Trio of Suriname, the Waimiri-Atroari and Hixkaryana of Brazil, the Karijona of Colombia and the Yukpa. Hixkaryana is famous among linguists: its usual word order is object, verb, subject, an order once thought not to exist.
